prompt:
Do crunch's calc threads all behave the same, or is one of them different? How?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: yes

## Difference across the calc threads

Across the whole trace (offsets **0–30,516 ms**), **calc-6 (TID 638178) is the standout**: it made **59,800 `write` calls**, while the other seven calc threads made **0**. The threads otherwise ran in parallel—an average of **7.53 of 8** were running whenever any calc thread ran.

Their per-round CPU work and mean finish times were fairly close:

| Thread | CPU work per round | Mean finish time |
|---|---:|---:|
| calc-0 | 10.359 ms | 10.444 ms |
| calc-1 | 10.231 ms | 10.363 ms |
| calc-2 | 10.363 ms | 10.488 ms |
| calc-3 | 10.191 ms | 10.300 ms |
| calc-4 | 10.252 ms | 10.372 ms |
| calc-5 | 10.230 ms | 10.366 ms |
| **calc-6** | **10.595 ms** | **10.739 ms** |
| calc-7 | 10.227 ms | 10.364 ms |

## Effect on crunch’s progress

In the same whole-trace window, **82.5%** of crunch’s waits on other threads ended when calc-6 woke it. The chain was crunch waiting on calc-6, which was doing its own CPU work. In one typical **10.662 ms** wait (starting at offset **10,194.178 ms**), calc-6 ran for **10.661 ms** after a **0.001 ms** preemption.

That difference is small as a process hold-up: calc-6 finished an average **0.220 ms** after its peers, about **2.0%** of a **10.739 ms** round. The rounds were consistent overall (median **10.725 ms**); **3** isolated rounds stood out.

TMLL reports **0 futex waits** for calc-6, despite **26,735.388 ms** total in futex calls: those waits are not what explains crunch’s waits on calc-6. Across the whole trace, all eight calc threads spent about **89–90%** of their time blocked, and each ran for about **10.2–10.6%** of its time.
